brief: The degree of knottedness of tangled vortex lines (Moffatt, J. Fluid Mech. 35 (1969) 117–129) — helicity as a topological invariant counting linking of vortex lines
extended:
**The degree of knottedness of tangled vortex lines** — H. K. Moffatt. J. Fluid Mech. 35, part 1 (1969) 117–129.

In an inviscid barotropic fluid the integral of u·ω over a region bounded by vortex surfaces (the helicity) is invariant. For a field confined to thin unknotted vortex filaments the invariant equals a sum over pairs of the linking numbers times the product of the circulations; a knotted filament is decomposed into linked unknotted ones, which gives a degree of knottedness. Sections treat solid boundaries, a consequence of the invariance, and the analogous magnetohydrodynamic invariant (magnetic helicity).

**Why it may bear here.** Registered as `moffatt1969`; cited in `helicity-conservation` and the knotted-particles history. It is the original of helicity = mutual linking, the fluid analogue of reading an interaction off linking numbers of closed components (cf. `procrsoclondona92`, Moffatt–Ricca 1992, on self-linking and the Călugăreanu invariant). Scanned original with a text layer: subscripts read as commas (C₁ appears as `C,`).
